title: Finite completed differentials and the completed conormal sequence
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] containing a subfield $F$ such that its residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m$ is a finite extension of the image of $F$. Write $\Omega_{A/F}$ for Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $M_F(A)=\varprojlim_n\Omega_{A/F}/\mathfrak m^n\Omega_{A/F}$, with the induced derivation $d_F:A\to M_F(A)$. Then $M_F(A)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], generated by elements $d_Fa$ with $a\in A$. For every finitely generated $\mathfrak m$-adically complete $A$-module $N$, composition with $d_F$ gives a bijection between $A$-linear maps $M_F(A)\to N$ and $F$-derivations $A\to N$. For each proper ideal $I\subset A$, the quotient $C=A/I$ is complete for $(\mathfrak m/I)$ and the canonical sequence
$$I/I^2\xrightarrow{\bar a\mapsto d_Fa\otimes1}M_F(A)\otimes_A C\longrightarrow M_F(C)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact (tensor products as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]). In particular, if $A$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotents) and $\mathfrak q$ is a minimal prime, the canonical map
$$M_F(A)\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak q)\longrightarrow M_F(A/\mathfrak q)\otimes_{A/\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak q)$$
is an isomorphism.

source.place: EGA 0_IV 20.7.14 (completed universal derivation), 20.7.15 and 21.9.1 (finite generation), 20.7.8 and 20.7.20 (completed quotient/conormal sequence; finite-module images are closed). The last assertion is the conormal sequence localized at a reduced minimal prime.

proof.text: Put $\Omega=\Omega_{A/F}$. Choose generators $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ of $\mathfrak m$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and an $F$-vector-space basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $k$, with lifts $a_j\in A$. The $\mathrm db_j$ generate $\Omega_{k/F}$: if $b=\sum c_jb_j$ with $c_j\in F$, the derivation rules in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] give $\mathrm db=\sum c_j\mathrm db_j$; every differential is a finite linear combination of such symbols by that definition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $F\to A\to k$. Its kernel is generated by the images of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, which in turn are generated by $\mathrm dt_i$ modulo $\mathfrak m\Omega$: write an element of $\mathfrak m$ as $\sum u_it_i$ and use $\mathrm d(\sum u_it_i)\equiv\sum u_i\mathrm dt_i\pmod{\mathfrak m\Omega}$. Its last map sends $\mathrm da_j$ to $\mathrm db_j$. Consequently $\Omega/\mathfrak m\Omega$ is generated over $k$ by the finite list of exact differentials $\mathrm dt_i,\mathrm da_j$.

source.place: 0_IV 20.7.15 and 21.9.1; ordinary conormal sequence is Stacks Tag 00RU, lemma-differential-seq

proof.text: Since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied to $\Omega$ identifies $M=M_F(A)$ modulo $\mathfrak m^n$ with $\Omega/\mathfrak m^n\Omega$ and makes $M$ complete and separated. The finite list from Step 1 therefore generates $M/\mathfrak mM$, and its lifts to $M$ are exactly $d_Ft_i,d_Fa_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] with ring $A$, ideal $\mathfrak m$ and module $M$: the ring is complete by hypothesis, separatedness is the preceding completion theorem, and finite generation modulo $\mathfrak m$ was just proved. The strengthened conclusion says these particular lifts generate $M$. This proves finiteness and generation by exact differentials, without assuming that the uncompleted $\Omega$ is finite.

source.place: Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring); the completion version of EGA 0_IV 20.7.15

proof.text: Let $N$ be as in the statement and let $D:A\to N$ be any $F$-derivation. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it corresponds to an $A$-linear map $h:\Omega\to N$. For each $n$, linearity gives $h(\mathfrak m^n\Omega)\subseteq\mathfrak m^nN$, so $h$ induces compatible maps $h_n:\Omega/\mathfrak m^n\Omega\to N/\mathfrak m^nN$. On compatible sequences define $\widehat h:M\to N$ by $\widehat h((x_n)_n)=(h_n(x_n))_n$, using the given bijection $N\cong\varprojlim_nN/\mathfrak m^nN$. This formula is $A$-linear and gives $\widehat h(d_Fa)=D(a)$. Conversely $d_F$ is a derivation, since its components are the ordinary universal derivation modulo $\mathfrak m^n$; thus composing any linear map with $d_F$ gives a derivation. Two such linear maps with the same composite agree on every $d_Fa$, hence on all of $M$ by Step 2. These constructions are inverse and prove exactly the asserted bijection, including derivations not initially assumed continuous.

source.place: 0_IV 20.7.14, the completion universal property; explicit compatible-sequence construction using the adic completion in the item

proof.text: Fix a proper ideal $I$. The module $C=A/I$ is generated over $A$ by $1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] makes it complete for the powers $\mathfrak m^nC=(\mathfrak m/I)^n$; here $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ since $A$ is local. It is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$: any element outside that ideal has a lift outside $\mathfrak m$ and hence a unit lift. It is Noetherian: the inverse image in $A$ of any ideal of $C$ is finitely generated, and the images of its generators generate the ideal. Also $F\to C$ is injective, because every nonzero element of the subfield $F\subset A$ is a unit and cannot lie in $I$. Its residue field is the same $k$, finite over $F$. Thus the arguments of Steps 1–3 apply to $C$ with these verified hypotheses; in particular $M_C=M_F(C)$ is finite over $C$, generated by $d_Cc$, and has the same derivation universal property for finite complete $C$-modules.

source.place: Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and its complete-ring corollary; EGA 0_IV 20.7.20, quotient ring completeness

proof.text: Let $P=M\otimes_A C$. By the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $P\cong M/IM$: the maps send $x\otimes\bar a$ to $ax\bmod IM$ and $x\bmod IM$ to $x\otimes1$, and are inverse on their generators. Set $\delta(a\bmod I^2)=d_Fa\otimes1$ for $a\in I$. It is well-defined and $C$-linear: for $a,b\in I$ the Leibniz formula $d_F(ab)=a\,d_Fb+b\,d_Fa$ vanishes in $P$, and for $u\in A$, $d_F(ua)\otimes1=\bar u(d_Fa\otimes1)$ since $a\,d_Fu\otimes1=0$. Let $H=\operatorname{im}\delta$ and $Q=P/H$. The quotient $Q$ is a finite $A$-module: the images of the finite generators of $M$ generate it. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian], $Q$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete, equivalently $(\mathfrak m/I)$-adically complete as a $C$-module. The map $a\mapsto[d_Fa\otimes1]$ to $Q$ is an $F$-derivation, zero on $I$, and therefore descends to $D_C:C\to Q$.

source.place: 0_IV 20.7.20; explicit conormal quotient construction as in Stacks Tag 00RU, lemma-differential-seq

proof.text: Apply the universal property proved in Step 3 for $C$ to $D_C$ with target $Q$, which is finite and complete by Step 5. It gives a $C$-linear map $v:M_C\to Q$ sending $d_C\bar a$ to $[d_Fa\otimes1]$. The derivation $A\to C\xrightarrow{d_C}M_C$ gives, by Step 3 for $A$, an $A$-linear map $M\to M_C$; this application is legitimate because $M_C$ is finite over $C$, hence over $A$, and is complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]. The map factors through $P$ since $I$ annihilates $M_C$, and then through $Q$ since it kills $d_Fa$ for $a\in I$. Call the resulting map $w:Q\to M_C$. The formulas show $wv(d_C\bar a)=d_C\bar a$ and $vw([d_Fa\otimes1])=[d_Fa\otimes1]$. Those elements generate their modules by Steps 2, 4 and 5, so $v,w$ are inverse. Hence the canonical map $P\to M_C$ is surjective with kernel $H$, which is precisely the required completed conormal sequence.

source.place: 0_IV 20.7.20; explicit universal-property proof of exactness once the modules and their quotients are finite complete

proof.text: Suppose $A$ is reduced and $\mathfrak q$ is minimal. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a field. Write $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak q)$. Fractions give a canonical identification $A_{\mathfrak q}=L$: $a/s\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$ is surjective, and if $a\in\mathfrak q$, then $a/1=0$ by $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}=0$, proving injectivity. Thus $(\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^2)\otimes_A L=0$. Explicitly, for any $a\in\mathfrak q$ there is $s\notin\mathfrak q$ with $sa=0$, so $(a\bmod\mathfrak q^2)\otimes\ell=(sa\bmod\mathfrak q^2)\otimes(\ell/s)=0$; these tensors generate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] over $C=A/\mathfrak q$ to the sequence of Step 6 with $I=\mathfrak q$, tensoring with $L$. Its left term is zero, so its middle-to-right map is bijective. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies the middle term with $M_F(A)\otimes_A L$ by $(x\otimes c)\otimes\ell\mapsto x\otimes c\ell$, inverse $x\otimes\ell\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes\ell$. The right term is $M_F(A/\mathfrak q)\otimes_{A/\mathfrak q}L$. On exact differentials the map sends $d_Fa\otimes\ell$ to $d_C\bar a\otimes\ell$, so it is the canonical map in the statement.

source.place: Tags 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring) and 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to the completed conormal sequence just established
